sections.h2: Where is Roswell and what is the city like?
sections.html:
Roswell is the county seat of Chaves County in southeastern New Mexico. It sits at about 3,615 feet, roughly 7 miles west of the Pecos River, with highlands rising toward the Sierra Blanca range some 40 miles to the west.

The city covers just under 30 square miles. It was founded in 1871 and incorporated on February 25, 1889, and the 2020 census counted 48,422 residents, which made it the fifth most populous city in the state. Chaves County makes up the whole Roswell micropolitan area, so the city is the regional center for shopping, health care and county government.

U.S. Routes 70, 285 and 380 pass through, and the Roswell International Air Center is the local airport. For a seller, the main effect of this setting is a smaller, more local pool of buyers than in a big metro. Local employers and the military school and college campuses shape who looks for a house here.

sections.h2: What is Roswell's history, and why does it matter to a home seller?
sections.html:
Roswell was a place of military importance from 1941 to 1967, and Walker Air Force Base was decommissioned in 1967. The Roswell Army Air Field handled the investigation and debris recovery for the 1947 incident that made the city's name famous, although the crash site was some 75 miles north near Corona.

In the 1930s, Robert H. Goddard did much of his early rocketry work in Roswell, and Goddard High School carries his name. Since 1997, an annual UFO Festival has marked the 50th anniversary of the 1947 event.

Why this matters when you sell: Roswell has been a settled city for well over a century, so many houses are old. An older house may have original wiring, plumbing or heating, and buyers and lenders ask about them. A cash buyer will usually take such a house as it is.

Roswell's economy mixes irrigated farming, dairying and ranching with manufacturing, distribution, petroleum-related facilities, education and tourism. A Leprino Foods mozzarella plant is among the best known manufacturers.

InstitutionWhat the sources say
New Mexico Military InstituteFounded in 1891, with high school and two-year college programs
Eastern New Mexico University-RoswellBranch campus with certificate and associate programs
Eastern New Mexico Medical Center162-bed community hospital
Leprino FoodsMozzarella manufacturing facility in Roswell

Tourism rests on ufology museums, including the International UFO Museum and Research Center, plus Americana travel. Bitter Lake National Wildlife Refuge lies a few miles northeast of the city, and Bottomless Lakes State Park is 12 miles east on U.S. 380.

sections.h2: How does Roswell's climate and flood history affect a house?
sections.html:
Roswell has a cold semi-arid climate with four distinct seasons. It averages 11.63 inches of precipitation a year and 9.6 inches of snow. The mean daily high runs from 56.5°F in December to 96.5°F in July, and the record range is from minus 24°F to 114°F. Heating and cooling systems both matter to a buyer.

Summer monsoon storms can bring torrential downpours, severe thunderstorms and sometimes tornadoes. Roswell also has a flood history from the Rio Hondo. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers records mass flooding in 1937, 1941 and 1954, which led to a flood control facility at Two Rivers Dam. The city posts FEMA flood information, including a March 23, 2012 map revision that shows dramatic changes to Hondo River floodplains.

  • Check the FEMA flood map for your address before you list.
  • Ask your insurance agent whether the home sits in a mapped floodplain.
  • Keep records of any roof, drainage or storm repairs.

sections.h2: Which schools and local rules matter when selling in Roswell?
sections.html:
The Roswell Independent School District serves the city, and Goddard High School is named for the rocket scientist. Roswell is also home to NMMI and an ENMU branch campus.

Code enforcement. The city's Code Enforcement Department works to keep Roswell a desirable place to live and do business. A City Council agenda from 2026 shows the council declaring structures to be dangerous buildings and public nuisances under Roswell Municipal Code section 16-12. If your house is vacant, damaged or neglected, a code complaint can reach you before a sale does, so clear any open notice first.

Permits. The city runs an online system for residential permits, with applications, email updates and inspection requests. Ask the city whether past work at your address was permitted.

sections.h2: How do Chaves County property taxes work in Roswell?
sections.html:
Chaves County handles property tax for Roswell addresses. Taxes go to several agencies, including the State of New Mexico, Chaves County, the Roswell Independent School District, ENMU-Roswell, the City of Roswell and the Flood Control Conservancy District.

DateWhat happens
January 1Valuation date for all taxable property
November 1Treasurer mails tax bills
November 10First half due
December 11Unpaid first half is delinquent
April 10Second half due
May 11Unpaid second half is delinquent
June 10Notices go out on taxes delinquent two years
July 1Treasurer sends the delinquent list to the State

The Chaves County Treasurer says that if delinquent taxes, penalty and interest are not paid within two years, the property records move to the State Property Tax Division, with a $125 cost to state fee and a risk of sale at public auction. Each county holds an annual auction in its commission chambers.

The Chaves County Assessor's office is at 1 St Mary's Place in Roswell, and the county's main number is 575-624-6600. A statewide rule gives owners 30 days after the Notice of Value is mailed to protest the value, and New Mexico's 2026 House Bill 285 restates that protest wording in the property tax code.

Under New Mexico law as summarized by Sandoval County, property taxes are a lien from January 1 of the tax year, and the owner of record on that date is responsible for that year's tax. If you sell in the spring, the buyer and seller usually settle the current year's tax through the contract, so ask the title company to show you how it is split on the closing statement.

sections.h2: What should a Roswell seller gather before talking to a buyer?
sections.html:
A short folder of documents speeds up any sale, whether it is a listing or a cash purchase.

  • Your latest Chaves County tax bill and proof of payment for both halves.
  • Any code enforcement notice, with the date and what it asked you to fix.
  • Receipts or permits for roof, plumbing, heating or storm repairs.
  • The FEMA flood zone for the address and any flood insurance policy.
  • For an inherited house, the death certificate and the probate or title paperwork.

Having these on hand lets a buyer give you a clear number sooner, and it protects you from surprises at the closing table.

sections.h2: What are your options for selling a Roswell house fast?
sections.html:
A Roswell owner can list the house, sell it directly, or take a cash offer, and the right choice depends on condition, timing and cost.

  • Listing: reaches the most buyers, but you pay for repairs, showings and closing costs.
  • Direct sale: avoids an agent but needs you to handle price, contract and paperwork.
  • Cash offer: comes from a buyer who purchases as-is. Always ask for it in writing and read the terms before signing.

Common reasons Roswell owners look at a cash sale are an inherited house, a vacant property attracting code notices, a flood or storm repair, tenants, or taxes that have fallen behind. Whatever route you choose, ask the title company how taxes and liens are handled at closing.

faqs.a: Roswell is in Chaves County and is its county seat. Chaves County forms the entire Roswell micropolitan area.

faqs.q: When are Chaves County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due November 10 and becomes delinquent December 11. The second half is due April 10 and becomes delinquent May 11. Bills are mailed by November 1.

faqs.q: Is Roswell at risk of flooding?
faqs.a: Parts of it have been. The Rio Hondo caused mass flooding in 1937, 1941 and 1954, and a flood control facility was built afterward. Check the city's FEMA flood information for your address.

faqs.q: What happens if I do not pay Roswell property taxes?
faqs.a: If taxes, penalty and interest stay unpaid for two years, the records move to the State Property Tax Division with a $125 cost to state fee, and the property can be sold at public auction.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Roswell house without making repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer purchases as-is, and you can also list it and negotiate with a buyer after inspection. Compare what you would net on each route.
